examInfo.title: JAMB Economics 2011 Past Questions
examInfo.subject: Economics
examInfo.instructions: Choose the correct option from A-D for each question.

questions.question: Which question paper type of economics is given to you?
questions.explanation: This question identifies the paper type for administrative purposes.

questions.question: An effective way of controlling inflation in a mixed economy is to
questions.explanation: Increasing productivity increases supply of goods and services, which helps control inflation by reducing price pressures.

questions.question: One of the limitations of PPC assumption is that there is

options.B: no recognition of preferred goods for countries

questions.explanation: The Production Possibility Curve assumes technology remains constant, which is a limitation as it doesn't account for technological progress.

questions.question: A major disadvantage of the arithmetic mean is that it is

options.B: not suitable for further statistical analysis
options.C: cumbersome to determine the actual value

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is heavily influenced by extreme values (outliers), which can distort the representation of the data.

questions.question: Demand patterns are determined by the market on the basis of
questions.explanation: Consumer sovereignty means consumers determine what goods are produced through their purchasing decisions, thus determining demand patterns.

questions.question: A consumer surplus measures the

options.A: benefits derived from consuming a cheap commodity
options.B: excess of total expenditure over total utility
options.C: difference between marginal utility and marginal cost
options.D: excess of marginal utility over price

questions.explanation: Consumer surplus is the difference between what consumers are willing to pay (marginal utility) and what they actually pay (price).

questions.question: If the demand for one commodity excludes another, it is said to be
questions.explanation: Competitive demand occurs when goods are substitutes, and the demand for one excludes or reduces demand for another.

questions.question: The graph of the schedule above will depict
questions.explanation: Based on the price-quantity relationship shown, this represents a normal downward-sloping demand curve.

questions.question: The median of an odd-numbered set of scores is the
questions.explanation: For an odd-numbered set of scores arranged in order, the median is the middle value.

questions.question: If demand increases without a change in supply, equilibrium price and quantity will
questions.explanation: When demand increases while supply remains constant, both equilibrium price and quantity will rise.

questions.question: In the process of production, total output is at maximum when
questions.explanation: Total output is maximized when marginal product (MP) equals zero, as any additional input would reduce total output.

questions.question: From the table above, the price elasticity of supply is
questions.explanation: Price elasticity of supply = (% change in quantity supplied)/(% change in price). Based on the given data, this equals 1.

questions.question: When a consumer is at equilibrium, the MRSxy is equal to the
questions.explanation: At consumer equilibrium, the marginal rate of substitution (MRSxy) equals the ratio of the prices of the two goods (Px/Py).

questions.question: Minimum price legislation by government will
questions.explanation: Minimum price (price floor) set above equilibrium reduces quantity demanded and creates a surplus.

questions.question: Ranking is the method used in measuring
questions.explanation: Ordinal utility uses ranking to order preferences without measuring exact utility levels.

questions.question: If a firm is faced with an elastic supply curve, its revenue will

options.A: be supplied at a higher price
options.C: increase by more than the percentage increase in price

questions.explanation: With elastic supply, quantity supplied responds more than proportionally to price changes, leading to revenue increases greater than the price increase percentage.

questions.question: The optimal range of output for a perfectly competitive firm is
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm operates optimally where marginal cost is rising and equals marginal revenue.

questions.question: A firm will experience diseconomies of scale when

options.A: there are difficulties in coordinating production
options.B: there is shortage in labour supply
options.C: the size of market is small
options.D: there is an increase in the price of raw materials

questions.explanation: Diseconomies of scale occur when firms become too large to manage efficiently, leading to coordination difficulties.

questions.question: The law of variable proportions is applicable only
questions.explanation: The law of variable proportions (diminishing returns) applies in the short run when at least one factor is fixed.

questions.question: From the diagram above, the optimal point of production is
questions.explanation: Based on the production diagram, point S represents the optimal production point.

questions.question: If real income increases while nominal income remains the same, it can be inferred that
questions.explanation: If nominal income stays constant but real income increases, it means prices have fallen, increasing purchasing power.

questions.question: One of the characteristics of oligopoly is the availability of
questions.explanation: Oligopoly is characterized by a market with few sellers who have significant market power.

questions.question: The average total cost when 20 units are produced is
questions.explanation: Based on the cost diagram provided, the average total cost at 20 units of output is ₦15.00.

questions.question: When 20 units of output is produced, TC will be
questions.explanation: Total Cost = Average Total Cost × Quantity = ₦15 × 20 = ₦300

questions.question: The profit of a monopolist can be eliminated where price equals
questions.explanation: A monopolist's profit is eliminated when price equals average cost (AC), resulting in normal profit only.

questions.question: Bank consolidation policy in Nigeria is a measure to increase
questions.explanation: Bank consolidation policy aims to increase the capital base of banks to make them more stable and competitive.

questions.question: An increase in the circulation of money without a corresponding increase in output will lead to
questions.explanation: When money supply increases without corresponding increase in output, it leads to inflation as more money chases the same goods.

questions.question: In national income accounts, an item counted as part of government spending is
questions.explanation: Salaries and wages paid by government are counted as government spending in national income accounts.

questions.question: If aggregate demand is lower than total output in an economy national income will
questions.explanation: When aggregate demand is less than total output, there is excess supply, leading to a fall in national income.

questions.question: During the era of barter, money was generally in the form of
questions.explanation: In the barter era, commodities like cattle, grains, and shells served as money before the development of metallic money.

questions.question: A country achieves economic development when there is

options.C: a sustained increase in per capita income
options.D: an even distribution of goods and services

questions.explanation: Economic development is characterized by sustained increases in per capita income, indicating improved living standards.

questions.question: An indicator of growth in an economy over a period of time is the
questions.explanation: GDP at market price is the most commonly used indicator to measure economic growth over time.

questions.question: A country embarks on deficit financing in order to
questions.explanation: Deficit financing is used to stimulate investment and economic activity by increasing government spending beyond revenue.

questions.question: The deflationary gap is defined by
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, X represents the deflationary gap.

questions.question: What does X represent?
questions.explanation: X represents the deflationary gap in the macroeconomic diagram.

questions.question: The import-substitution strategy of industrialization is to encourage
questions.explanation: Import substitution strategy aims to encourage domestic production to replace imported goods.

questions.question: Upstream oil activities involve the
questions.explanation: Upstream oil activities involve exploration and extraction of crude oil from the ground.

questions.question: Agricultural production in Nigeria is constrained by
questions.explanation: Poor implementation of agricultural policies has been a major constraint to agricultural production in Nigeria.

questions.question: The main function of NNPC is to

options.A: oversee the development of the oil sector

questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) oversees the development and regulation of Nigeria's oil sector.

questions.question: Investing heavily in the agricultural sector will lead to
questions.explanation: Heavy investment in agriculture primarily leads to sufficient food production to meet domestic needs.

questions.question: Industrial development in Nigeria can be encouraged through
questions.explanation: Efficient infrastructure is crucial for industrial development as it reduces production and transportation costs.

questions.question: The record of a country's transactions in international trade is her
questions.explanation: Balance of payments records all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world.

questions.question: The transfer of public shareholding corporations to private enterprises is
questions.explanation: Privatization is the transfer of ownership of public enterprises to private entities.

questions.question: A condition in which official and autonomous exchange rate coexist is
questions.explanation: Multiple exchange rate system exists when there are different official and autonomous exchange rates operating simultaneously.

questions.question: In modern economies, the Malthusian theory of population is ineffective because of
questions.explanation: Technical progress has increased food production capacity, making Malthusian predictions about population outgrowing food supply less relevant.

questions.question: Optimum population enables an economy to attain the highest level of
questions.explanation: Optimum population is the population size that maximizes income per head (per capita income).

questions.question: A change from one industry to another by a worker is an example of
questions.explanation: Horizontal mobility refers to movement between different industries or occupations at the same skill level.

questions.question: The money paid per hour for work done is
questions.explanation: Wage rate is the amount paid per unit of time (hour) for work performed.

questions.question: Trade takes place because of
questions.explanation: International trade occurs because countries have comparative advantages in producing different goods.

questions.question: The World Trade Organization is responsible for

options.B: ensuring equal participation of countries in trade
options.D: minimizing obstacles to international trade and investment

questions.explanation: The WTO's primary function is to reduce barriers and obstacles to international trade and investment.
